{{Top}}
[[File:Jawas_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A band of [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]] scavengers.]]
{{Quote|They wait in the wings, too weak to participate, but patient, knowing that at some point the fighting will cease and then they can swoop in to take what they will ...|[[Rivoche Tarkin]]|<ref name="desb">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
A '''scavenger''' or '''salvager''', often abbreviated "'''scav''',"<ref name="desb" /><ref name="rc">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref> was a person or [[Droid/Legends|droid]] whose primary occupation was collecting lost or abandoned items or recovering wreckage from disaster or battle sites.

==History==
{{Quote|Just so, in all wars there are people who exploit the carnage for their own gain. This is no different now, as Empire and Republic clash, than it was millennia ago during the chaos of Xim's reign.|Rivoche Tarkin|<ref name="desb" />}}
[[File:Gha_Nachkt_Discount.png|thumb|left|250px|[[Gha Nachkt/Legends|Gha Nachkt]], a Trandoshan scavenger]]
Some [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] were predominantly scavengers, such as [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]], [[Teek/Legends|Teeks]]<ref name="ISWU">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref>, and [[Ugor/Legends|Ugors]].<ref name="schu">[[Scavenger Hunt (adventure)|''Scavenger Hunt'']].</ref> It was also a common occupation for [[Human/Legends|Humans]] and [[near-Human]]s.<ref name="kotor2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> Though many scavengers were honorable, the term "scav" or "scavver" was sometimes used as an insult.<ref name="leg14">[[Legacy (2006) 14|''Legacy'' (2006) 14]]</ref>

[[Meetra Surik]] encountered some small [[Salvager camp|camps]] of salvagers on the planet [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]], who tried to live by selling the [[Jedi artifact/Legends|Jedi artifacts]] they had found in the ruins of the [[Jedi Enclave]] in the years after [[Darth Malak]]'s [[Attack on Dantooine (Jedi Civil War)|attack]].<ref name="kotor2" /> These salvagers generally held beings with regular jobs in contempt, and would have been particularly pleased if the settlers had been driven off the planet.<ref name="kotor2ds">In ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'', if [[Meetra Surik]] takes the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] path and sides with [[Azkul]], the salvagers remain on the world and gloat about the settlers' loss. It is therefore possible to infer that they would enjoy this turn of events even if it did not canonically occur.</ref>

[[P-100 salvage droid|Salvage droids]] were commonly used to collect debris at [[Podracing/Legends|podraces]] during the last decades of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="ep1">{{Film|I}}</ref> Other [[Salvage droid/Legends|scavenger droids]] were less benign, and were used by [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshans]] to kill people and "scavenge" their corpses.<ref name="rc" />

During the height of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], salvagers that wished to operate needed to register with the [[Imperial Trade and Commerce Authority]]. This company was notoriously bureaucratic and receiving the proper permits from them could take months and sometimes even years. Additionally, if a salvager wished to work under the Empire, they would have to submit to an extensive background check. These requirements sometimes lead to aspiring scavengers to forge the proper permits.<ref name="DH">{{JournalCite|9|Death-Hunter}}, p. 204</ref>

Particularly aggressive scavengers operated in the immediate aftermath of the [[Imperial Civil War]], some of whom maintained small private armies to assist in their operations.<ref name="de1">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]''</ref>
